Question: Describe the current responsibilities of all three teams, and explain the org changes that produced this structure, step by step.

**Current Team Responsibilities** | Team | Primary Scope (What they own) | Typical Activities | |------|------------------------------|--------------------| | **Frontend** | All client‑facing software that runs in the user’s browser or on a mobile device. | • UI/UX design implementation
• Component libraries, styling, and accessibility
• Client‑side state management and routing
• Integration with Backend APIs (consumption, error handling, caching)
• Front‑end testing (unit, integration, visual regression)
• Performance monitoring of page load, bundle size, runtime metrics | | **Backend** | Business‑logic services and public APIs that expose the product’s core functionality. | • Design and implementation of domain‑level services
• Data‑validation, transformation, and orchestration
• CRUD and complex query handling against data stores
• Authentication/authorization (business‑level policies)
• API versioning, documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger)
• Service‑level testing, contract testing, monitoring of latency & error rates | | **Platform** | The underlying infrastructure, tooling, and operational processes that enable the Frontend and Backend teams to ship and run software reliably. | • Cloud‑resource provisioning (compute, storage, networking)
• CI/CD pipeline design, maintenance, and automation
• Container orchestration / serverless runtime management
• Observability stack (metrics, logs, tracing) and alerting
• Security hardening of the environment (IAM, secrets management, patching)
• Cost‑optimization, capacity planning, disaster‑recovery procedures | All three teams continue to operate under normal, “standard‑conditions” production environments: routine maintenance is performed on schedule, no abnormal incidents have been reported, and all key health metrics remain within expected ranges. --- ## Step‑by‑Step Evolution of the Organization | Phase | Org Structure | Why the Change Was Made | Resulting Team Focus | |-------|---------------|------------------------|----------------------| | **Phase 1 – Single “Full‑Stack” Team** | One team responsible for **both** client‑side (frontend) and server‑side (backend) work. | Early stage of the company – limited headcount, product still small, so a single cross‑functional group could cover everything efficiently. | The team owned the entire stack (UI, business logic, infrastructure basics). | | **Phase 2 – Split into Frontend & Backend** | Two dedicated teams: **Frontend** and **Backend**. | Rapid growth in product complexity and user base created a need for deeper specialization. Separate skill sets (UI/UX vs. domain logic) could be cultivated, and delivery cadence could increase without one side blocking the other. | • Frontend team took full ownership of everything that runs in the user’s browser/device.
• Backend team took ownership of business‑logic services, APIs, and data handling. | | **Phase 3 – Carve Out a Platform Team from Backend** | Three teams: **Frontend**, **Backend**, **Platform**. | The Backend team’s scope kept expanding (more services, higher traffic, stricter reliability requirements). Managing cloud resources, CI/CD, monitoring, and security began to consume a significant portion of the Backend engineers’ time, pulling focus away from core business logic. A dedicated Platform group was created to own the shared infrastructure and tooling. | • Backend team narrowed its focus to **business logic & APIs only** (no longer responsible for infra).
• Platform team assumed all infrastructure, DevOps, and reliability responsibilities.
• Frontend team remained unchanged, continuing its client‑side focus. | ### Summary of the Organizational Flow 1. **Initial State** – One full‑stack team does everything. 2. **Growth Trigger** – Product and user‑base expansion → need for specialization. 3. **First Re‑org** – Split into **Frontend** (UI/UX) and **Backend** (services & APIs). 4. **Further Scaling** – Backend’s operational burden (cloud, CI/CD, monitoring) grows → **Platform** team is spun out of Backend. 5. **Current State** – Three focused teams with clear, non‑overlapping responsibilities as listed above. This step‑wise separation has allowed each team to deepen expertise in its domain, improve delivery speed, and maintain the “standard‑conditions” operating environment that the organization has reported throughout each phase.
